## What's new (event happened Sept 23–24, 2026, Menlo Park)

Meta held its Connect 2026 keynote on **September 23, 2026**, with coverage still rolling out as of Sept 24-25. Key announcements:

**Hardware (four new devices):**
- Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 3) glasses — a refresh with longer battery life and a few new frame styles, available today starting at $449.
- Ray-Ban Meta Audio — Meta's first pair of camera-free glasses, shipping October 13, pre-order starting at $349. It comes in the Clubmaster and Burbank styles.
- Meta VR Glasses — a new ultra-thin VR headset aimed at entertainment and productivity, costing $1,299 and available this spring. All computing is handled by a tethered puck running Qualcomm's Snapdragon Reality Elite chipset, delivering "up to three hours of continuous high-resolution media playback" with support for 45W fast charging.
- Muse Charm — an AI device holding an AI agent on your keychain, available this fall, though pricing hasn't been announced yet.

**AI/software:**
- Muse AI was announced to work with a host of retailers, including Walmart and Instacart, for making purchases on your behalf.
- Meta is bringing Muse to its glasses so users can connect with their agent throughout the day.
- By the end of this year there will be over 100 styles of AI glasses.
- Meta also debuted "hologram," a photorealistic, real-time digital representation of you for video calls, created with just a quick self-capture on your phone.

**Accessibility feature:**
- Meta's supported smart glasses are now FDA-certified hearing aids for people with mild to moderate hearing loss, with a one-time $149 purchase to unlock permanent "medical-grade hearing" enhancement.

**Gaming/VR ecosystem:**
- At launch there will be 75 games playable via hand gestures, with full compatibility for existing Quest games via Touch Plus controllers, plus Xbox Cloud Gaming streaming support.
- Beat Saber is getting its biggest update yet this spring, evolving into a multi-mode rhythm platform on Meta VR Glasses and Quest.

## Meta Connect 2026: What Changed, Exact Figures, and Context

**Event basics:** Meta held its Connect 2026 keynote at company headquarters in Menlo Park, California, on Wednesday, September 23, 2026 (https://insideai.news/news/ai-hardware-infrastructure/meta-ai-glasses-muse/12768/). Meta unveiled its most aggressive push into wearable AI at its annual Connect conference in Menlo Park, California, on Wednesday, September 23 (https://insideai.news/news/ai-hardware-infrastructure/meta-ai-glasses-muse/12768/).

### 1. Four New Hardware Devices

**Meta VR Glasses** — the headline hardware reveal:
- The main highlight was the Meta VR Glasses, a $1,300 tethered headset scheduled for release next spring (https://www.medianama.com/2026/09/223-meta-connect-vr-glasses-muse-ai-keychain/). Exact price confirmed elsewhere as $1,299.99 (https://thenextweb.com/news/meta-vr-glasses-hearing-aid-connect-2026).
- Meta states the device weighs approximately 100 grams, about one-fifth the weight of a Quest 3 glasses. It features a magnesium alloy frame with pancake lenses. The VR glasses offer color passthrough and a 5K display (https://www.medianama.com/2026/09/223-meta-connect-vr-glasses-muse-ai-keychain/).
- It is the first VR device to receive IMAX Enhanced certification. The device also supports Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos (https://www.medianama.com/2026/09/223-meta-connect-vr-glasses-muse-ai-keychain/).
- A tethered puck handles all processing using Qualcomm's Snapdragon Reality Elite chip and contains both storage and the battery (https://www.medianama.com/2026/09/223-meta-connect-vr-glasses-muse-ai-keychain/).
- The glasses run on Qualcomm's Snapdragon Reality Elite chipset and offer up to three hours of continuous high-resolution media playback per charge. The puck supports 45W fast charging (https://dataconomy.com/2026/09/24/what-happened-at-meta-connect-2026/).
- The glasses feature a 5K micro-OLED display with 37 pixels per degree, pancake lenses, Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos audio (https://www.gizbot.com/accessories/features/meta-connect-2026-meta-vr-glasses-ray-ban-meta-gen-3-and-more-announced-128739.html).
- Meta said 75 games will be playable at launch with hand gestures. The glasses will also support all Quest games through Touch Plus controllers, Xbox Cloud Gaming, and wireless connections (https://dataconomy.com/2026/09/24/what-happened-at-meta-connect-2026/).

**Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3**:
- Announced at Meta Connect 2026, the third-generation glasses start at $449 in the US, $70 more than their predecessor's original launch price (https://thepcenthusiast.com/ray-ban-meta-gen-3-price-features/).
- Meta confirmed a single 12MP camera, 3K Ultra HD video, a six-microphone array, up to nine hours of battery life and a customizable action button (https://dymesty.com/blogs/articles/meta-ray-ban-gen-3-connect-2026).
- The Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3, available immediately for $449, refreshes the existing camera frame with a slimmer chassis, a six-microphone array that Meta says reduces background noise by over 90 percent (https://www.stylerave.com/meta-connect-2026/).
- Buyers can choose between the Aviator, Zena and Wayfarer, with 27 color and lens combinations available across the collection (https://thepcenthusiast.com/ray-ban-meta-gen-3-price-features/).

**Ray-Ban Meta Audio** — Meta's first camera-free glasses:
- The Ray-Ban Meta Audio are Meta's first glasses focused primarily on audio. They use open-ear speakers and weigh 43g, with Clubmaster and Burbank frame styles available across 23 frame and lens combinations. Prescription lens support is also included. The glasses feature adjustable temple tips, interchangeable nose pads and overextension hinges (https://www.gizbot.com/accessories/features/meta-connect-2026-meta-vr-glasses-ray-ban-meta-gen-3-and-more-announced-128739.html).
- They are available for pre-order now at $349 and ship October 13 (https://www.stylerave.com/meta-connect-2026/).
- Meta's product page states plainly that it is "built without a camera," and the camera rows of Meta's own comparison table are empty (https://bestinxr.com/post/meta-connect-2026-everything-announced).

**Muse Charm**:
- Meta revealed a Tamagotchi-style standalone gadget called the Muse Charm. This small handheld device is equipped with a screen, speaker, microphone, and a fingerprint sensor. It acts as a dedicated, physical home for the Muse AI agent to manage calendars, run errands, and handle email on the go without needing to wake a phone (https://sundayguardianlive.com/tech-news/meta-connect-2026-highlights-from-new-camera-free-ai-ray-ban-meta-audio-glasses-to-vr-glasses-more-here-are-7-biggest-announcements-expected-availability-291843/).
- Zuckerberg says it's not finalized yet, but they are planning to have it ship "in time for the holidays" in December, calling it Muse Charm (https://www.engadget.com/2266105/meta-connect-2026-live-blog-ai-vr/).
